full_judgment: 3. The defendant No. 1 and 6 appeared in the suit but defendant No. 6, thereafter, did not contest the suit. The defendant No. 1 above petitioner, contested the suit by filing written statement and denied the material allegations made in the plaint and stated inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable; that the plaintiff has no cause of action; that the suit is barred by the principles of estoppels, waiver and acquiescence and the suit is barred by limitation and stated further that the suit schedule land originally belong to Kumud Behari who died leaving 3(three) sons namely Benoy Behari Mahanto, Renu Bhuson Mahanto and Dhirendra Mohanto. Dhirendra died leaving 2(two) daughters Kalpana Ram and Shapna Rani. The heirs of Kumud Behari by amicable partition have been possessing the suit land. While Renu Bhuson was in possession of his share made the deed of gift of the schedule land in favour of the defendant No.1 by registered deed of gift dated 19.3.1994 and delivered possession and the said gift is not of forged deed and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.
